# Phase One — Deployment Hardening Recovery

The Awtsmoos renews every finite release vessel each instant. This wave touches deployment infrastructure only; the 115-test application release remains frozen.

## Boundless possibilities
- Identify the exact remote phase that fails without exposing credentials.
- Make every remote phase name itself before execution.
- Add a safe ERR trap that prints phase, exit code, repo path, branch, HEAD and fetched origin/main SHA only.
- Keep secrets out of logs entirely.
- Separate transient network fetch failure from permanent production-repo state failure.
- Retry only idempotent network operations such as `git fetch`, never activation blindly.
- Verify the production repo is a Git worktree and identify branch/detached state explicitly.
- Avoid assuming branch `main` is checked out if exact-SHA reset is the real invariant.
- Verify expected SHA exists locally before reset.
- Preserve exact-SHA hard-reset/clean semantics.
- Verify activation script contract before changing branch assumptions.
- Give canonical activation a named phase and retain its current behavior.
- Run home and tunnel public verifiers as distinct named phases.
- Add a lightweight release canary after activation if existing verifiers do not cover Wallet routing.
- Preserve concurrency serialization and no-force Git release behavior.
- Keep workflow compact by moving remote shell logic into a small tested script if this improves diagnosability.
- Make deployment helper locally testable in a dry-run/preflight mode without production credentials.
- Keep every touched script under 120 lines and fully documented.
- Push only from the isolated release worktree after syntax, dry-run, and Git freshness gates.
- Verify the GitHub Action and the live reconciliation canary after deployment.
